lawyer: SAM Mahbub Elahi, Advocate ----- For the Appellants.
parties:
Bashi alias Bashir and another ----- Appellants
Vs.
The State ----- Respondent
full_judgment:
This application under section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1908 is for condonation of delay in filing criminal Appeal No. 486 of 1989 under section 30 of the Special Powers Act; 1974 from an order of conviction and sentence dated 21.1.1989 passed by the Special Tribunal No. 2, Narayanganj, convicting and sentencing the petitioners to suffer RI for 3 years each under section 4(c) and 4B of the Cruelty to Women (Deterrent Punishment) Ordinance, 1983 and absconding accused Nurul Islam and Shaha Alam were sentenced to suffer RI for 10 years for the offence punishable under section 4(c) with the direction that the sentence imposed under those sections shall run concurrently in Special Tribunal Case No. 21 of 1988. 

 2. Mr. SAMM Elahi submits that although section 30 prescribes30 days for filing an appeal from an Order of the Special Tribunal his clients are entitled to get the benefit of section 5 of the Limitation Act. Mr. Elahi relied upon some decisions of Indian Jurisdiction. In those decisions section 5 of the Limitation Act was not considered vis-a-vis Special Powers Act, 1974 at all. Suffice it to refer the decision in the case of Vidyacharan Vs. Khubchand, AIR 1964 (SC) 1099. Mr. Elahi referred me to paragraphs 9 and 10 of the aforesaid decision and made an attempt to build up his contention that section 29(2) of the Limitation Act does not exclude the section 5. According to him, clause (a) of sub-section (2) of section 29 makes section 5 of the Limitation Act applicable to section 30 of the Special Powers Act inasmuch as section 5 of the Limitation Act has not been expressly excluded by the Special Powers Act. In Vidayacharan no such question fell for consideration before the Supreme Court of India as is now argued by Mr. Elahi before me. The principle laid down in that case has no application to the instant case. The .point mooted before me exactly came up before a Single Bench of this Court in the case of Mustafa alias Mustafizur Rahman Vs. The State reported in 1985 BLD 335. In that case Md. Altaf Hossain, J., was of the view that an appellant filing a time barred appeal under section 30 of Special Powers Act can invoke the provision of section 5 of the Limitation Act if the Court is satisfied that there was sufficient cause for the appellant not to prefer the appeal within 30 days from the date of the order of the Special Tribunal as prescribed under section 30 of the Act. But in the case of Elahi Box Vs. The State 1987 BLD 126 a Division Bench of this Division took a. contrary view. The Division Bench after taking into consideration sections 4, 9 to 18, 22 and section 29 (2) of the Limitation Act concluded that an appellant is not entitled to the benefit of section 5 of Limitation Act when the appeal under section 30 of the Special Powers Act is barred by limitation. The decision has also been followed in several decisions of this Division. In view of the decision made by the Division Bench in Elahi Baksh it is difficult for me to make a departure from the same sitting in a Single Bench. As the point raised before me is covered by the decision in Elahi Baksh, I am constrained to hold that contention of Mr. Elahi is of no substance.
